additionalProperties.kizunaNote: Scalar column values only. C-4: JSON numbers are non-negative integers < 2^31; every int64-class value rides as a decimal string (DR:cursor-and-sequence-decimal-string-grammar); floats and exponents never appear in the corpus.

oneOf.kizunaNote: Postgres array columns (D-field-transforms arrayUnion/arrayRemove) encode as JSON arrays of scalars. Not a C-4 exception: C-4 still forbids floats and negative JSON numbers.

column_values.kizunaNote: A { column: value } map whose key set IS the column mask (P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution 'masked columns'). Invariant I-6 requires every column to exist in fixtures/domain.json.

cursor.kizunaNote: Normative concept: an opaque token encoding the last fully applied server sequence (P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution). D-cursor-opaque-token selected a decimal high-water mark, optionally '~' plus ascending dot-separated holes. A continuation page prefixes '<start>:', the high-water of the checkpoint its transfer started from, and CHECKPOINT_EXPIRED checks that start; a checkpoint token carries none. The SQL pack emits no holes because its sequence numbers are commit-ordered, the refined reference oracle may emit them, and every codec accepts every form. Cursor '0' means bootstrap, and seq fields stay strictly decimal.

iso_timestamp.kizunaNote: Logical timestamp grammar (C-8 schema-enforced): 2026-01-01T00:00:SS.000Z, SS = logical step seconds, strictly increasing per transcript for server-assigned fields.

mutation.kizunaNote: The outbox unit: mutation_id, table, pk, op, masked columns, base_hint.

base_hint.kizunaNote: Named by P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution, shape and semantics undefined anywhere, this schema slot permits any value; NO seed transcript uses it.

columns.kizunaNote: The column mask is the key set (P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution 'masked columns'); empty for op delete.

hlc.kizunaNote: Optional origin HLC. Arrival-mode tables do not use it for ordering; hlc-mode tables use it for per-column origin-order resolution. conflict/003 exercises the field and SUPERSEDED outcome. Wire grammar: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision and a Z suffix, a decimal logical counter, a node id, joined by '|'.

precondition.kizunaNote: Optional Bayou-style expected column-mask values (P:verdict-completeness-transforms-and-conflict-rejection); mismatch ⇒ rejected(PRECONDITION).

transforms.kizunaNote: Optional field transforms on op:update only (D-field-transforms). Key MUST NOT also appear in columns. Always applied at the arbiter; not HLC-compared. Omitted when empty.

rowKey.kizunaNote: The row key text (D-row-key). A synced table's key columns are its primary-key columns in index order. With one key column the pk is that column's value as Postgres to_jsonb renders it: a lowercase hyphenated uuid, a plain decimal integer with an optional leading minus, or text unchanged. With several it is the JSON array of those texts, every one a JSON string, in the Postgres jsonb text form: '[', the components joined by ', ', then ']', escaping only '"', '\', and U+0000 to U+001F (\b \f \n \r \t, otherwise \u00XX in lowercase hex), so ["1", "3456"]. The engine derives it on the device and the SQL pack in its triggers, from the same vectors (vectors/row-key-vectors.json); hosts never compute it. A corpus pk that is a uuid still follows the placeholder grammar of $defs/uuid.

row_change.kizunaNote: Latest state only: Postgres-is-the-snapshot, no row-image oplog (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints). Rows may carry attachment references as ordinary column values; attachment bytes never ride this channel (P:attachments-are-out-of-protocol-scope, AT:media-attachments). The current corpus domain has no attachment column.

row.kizunaNote: The full latest row state visible under the caller's RLS. The public RPC is SECURITY DEFINER for private bookkeeping, but delegates user-row reads to a SECURITY DEFINER helper owned by the non-BYPASSRLS kizunasync_rls role with the caller's JWT claims.

seq.kizunaNote: Server-assigned sequence from one global sequence shared by all synced tables, drawn when the writing transaction commits (P:session-guarantees-and-exactly-once-effect mechanism 1; SQL:global-change-sequence). Decimal string on the wire (DR:cursor-and-sequence-decimal-string-grammar 'protocol state stored as TEXT everywhere'). Decimal seq and cursor token: dense from '1' per transcript except fencing cases (gaps by design).

signal.kizunaNote: Signal names are normative (P:cursor-monotonicity-rebase-and-atomic-checkpoints). D-signal-excludes-page-data ratified the exclusive shape enforced by invariant I-8: a non-null signal means empty rows and tombstones with has_more false.

type.kizunaNote: CHECKPOINT_EXPIRED: cursor predates oldest retained tombstone ⇒ client re-hydrates via keyset pagination. RESET_REQUIRED: client schema_version below the configured minimum ⇒ soft-block (P:schema-version-signalling).

table_name.kizunaNote: Synced user-table name. Invariant I-6 additionally requires membership in fixtures/domain.json.

tombstone.kizunaNote: Tombstone field set: (table, pk, seq, deleted_at), written by AFTER DELETE trigger and reaped past TTL; TTL interacts with checkpoint expiry.

transform.kizunaNote: Closed field-transform menu (D-field-transforms). increment.by is a signed integer: schema exception to C-4 (C-4 non-negative ints stay on column_values). JSON number when |n| < 2^31, else decimal string.

uuid.kizunaNote: Production wire values are RFC-4122 UUIDs; the corpus pins placeholder grammar: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-KKNNNNNNNNNN with kind codes a1 user · c1 client · e1 row pk · f1 mutation. Invariant I-6 requires registration in fixtures/identifiers.json.

verdict.kizunaNote: The union is normative: applied | rejected(reason, server_row) (P:mutations-and-column-masked-conflict-resolution Verdict, Realm compensating-writes lineage). D-verdict-correlation ratified dual correlation by request order and mutation_id, and invariant I-5 enforces the bijection for verdict responses.

oneOf.kizunaNote: applied ⇒ the client clears the outbox entry (P:verdict-completeness-transforms-and-conflict-rejection).

server_row.kizunaNote: Optional. Required when any mutation.transforms ran (D-field-transforms) so the client can snap optimistic local state to the arbiter total. Omitted on ordinary assigns.

oneOf.kizunaNote: A rejected verdict drives a compensating revert to server_row plus a typed event (P:verdict-completeness-transforms-and-conflict-rejection).

reason.kizunaNote: Closed union (D-rejection-reasons). RLS_DENIED also covers a non-insert against an absent or caller-hidden row because an RLS-scoped server must not leak which case occurred (push/006). CONSTRAINT is a class-23 or class-22 error, a P0001, or a 428C9 (a value for a column generated always), raised while the mutation's row is applied, and rejects that mutation alone; DELETE_WINS rejects edits of tombstoned rows; SUPERSEDED means every masked column lost the hlc-mode comparison (conflict/003). COLUMN_DENIED refuses a mutation that writes a column the caller's role may not write; server_row carries the readable columns.

server_row.kizunaNote: The row for the compensating revert (P:verdict-completeness-transforms-and-conflict-rejection). D-rejection-reasons ratified null when the row is caller-invisible under RLS or deleted; delete-wins therefore reverts to local absence.

kizunaNote: Shared $defs for the corpus. Intra-corpus $ref values are either #/$defs/<name> or common.schema.json#/$defs/<name>, resolved against the union of these $defs and the validating schema's own $defs (harness/ajv-validate.ts).
